plan.rationale: Initial baseline plan for gemm_128x4096x4096 (M=128,N=4096,K=4096). Domains chosen so tiles divide M/N/K: block_M in {16,32,64,128} divides 128; block_N in {32,64,128,256} divides 4096; block_K in {32,64,128} divides 4096. num_stages 1-4 and threads 64/128/256 included for exploration, but swizzle restricted to [0] to establish a conventional row-major baseline as instructed. Shared limit 32768 (also within the hard portability cap) to keep register/shared pressure conservative for Metal/GB10 portability; estimate = max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages, 4*block_M*block_N) will bind for large tiles at high stages. Equal weights 1 for traffic, launches, pipeline, footprint to get an unbiased first ranking. Note M has a single tile row for block_M=128, so swizzle reuse gains are moot there; larger N tiles reduce launches but increase footprint, and smaller block_M may add parallelism. Next hypothesis after baseline: perturb thread domain (e.g., 256) and block_K (e.g., 128) to test register/pipeline trade-offs, then expand swizzle to [0,4,8,16,32,64] once row-major baseline is measured.

Baseline attempt-00 passed numerics, compiled, and simulated at 157.29 us with block_M=128, block_N=64, block_K=64, num_stages=1, threads=256, swizzle=0, smem=32768 bytes (at cap), 2 blocks/SM. M=128 means block_M=128 gives a single tile row, so panel swizzle reuse is moot there; retain block_M=16/32/64/128 to allow multi-row panels and parallelism. Keep block_N up to 256 (divides 4096) to test larger-N-launch trade-off, but drop 32 to focus. block_K includes 128 to probe the pipeline/register trade-off; num_stages raised to 2-4 (stage=1 gave limited pipeline overlap and 2 blocks/SM). threads reduced to 128/256 since 64 was unmeasured and 256 worked; feedback will disambiguate. swizzle expanded to [0,4,8,16] modestly since large panels may exceed cache and M/Q small; restrict from 32/64 for first post-baseline run. Weight traffic at 1.5 (DRAM 34.6 MB dominates) and launches at 0.5 (only ~0.5-1k blocks), keep pipeline and footprint at 1; shared_memory_limit left at 32768 (hard portability cap binds anyway, actual smem hit cap). Next hypothesis: longer pipeline with stage=4 and block_K=128 improves simulation latency; test thread-domain change (128 vs 256) and modest swizzle now that a row-major baseline exists. Note validation scope: Metal numerics executed the exact source/config, CUDA binary not executed, GB10 values are simulator estimates only.

Two attempts observed: attempt-00 (block_M=128,block_N=64,block_K=64,stages=1,threads=256,swizzle=0) simulated 157.29us at smem=32768, 2 blocks/SM; attempt-01 (block_M=32,block_N=128,block_K=32,stages=3,threads=256,swizzle=16) was slower at 186.64us despite more blocks/SM (3) and lower registers, indicating the smaller block_M/block_K and deeper pipeline did not pay off - likely extra launch/tile count and swizzle panel not helping with this geometry. Both compiled, passed numerics/SMT. Since M=128 a single block_M=128 tile row gives no panel reuse benefit, so keep block_M domain broad including 64/128 to allow multi-row alternatives, but retain 16/32 only for parallelism probes. Keep block_N up to 256 to test wider N tiles that cut launches. Block_K includes 128 to probe longer per-stage work with fewer stages; stages limited to 2-4 because stage=1 underperformed vs stage=3 in attempt-01 pattern (though 00 was fastest). Threads kept 128/256 (64 unmeasured, 256 worked; 128 to test warp layout sensitivity). Swizzle now expanded to all allowed values [0,4,8,16,32,64] per post-baseline instruction, but full-sweep of swizzle alone is discouraged since M has few tile rows when block_M=128; combine with block_K=128 and stages=4 as the next hypothesis. Weights: reduce footprint to 0.75 (smem already at cap and not the bottleneck), raise pipeline to 1.5 to favor deeper overlap at block_K=64/128, keep traffic/launches at 1. Shared limit stays 32768 (hard portability cap). Next hypothesis: block_M=64/128 with block_N=128/256, block_K=128, stages=3-4, threads=128/256, testing whether larger tiles with deeper K-pipelining recover or beat the 157.29us baseline; validation scope note: Metal executed exact source/config/TIR numerics, CUDA binary not executed, GB10 latencies are simulator estimates only, not hardware measurements.

Three attempts observed: attempt-00 (block_M=128,block_N=64,block_K=64,stages=1,threads=256,swizzle=0) remains fastest at 157.29us, smem=32768, 2 blocks/SM. attempts-01/02 both selected block_M=32,block_N=128,block_K=32,stages=3,threads=256 with swizzle 16 then 64, simulated identically at 186.64us (same traffic 34.60MB, same blocks/SM=3); swizzle change produced no latency change, so the panel reuse proxy is not paying off here and small tiles/short block_K add launch overhead. Both compiled and passed numerics/SMT. Revision: drop block_M=16/32 and block_K=32 to stop re-selecting the losing small-tile regime, keeping block_M 64/128 and block_K 64/128 to test the untested larger-tile/deeper-K hypothesis; keep block_N up to 256 to probe fewer launches; stages 2-4 to explore overlap; threads 128/256 (256 worked, 128 untested for warp sensitivity). Swizzle trimmed to [0,4,8] since identical latency at 16/64 and M=128 gives at most 2 tile rows for block_M=64, so larger panels have no reuse headroom; avoid spending rounds on equivalent swizzles. Weights: footprint lowered to 0.6 (smem at cap but not the limiter), pipeline raised to 1.5 to favor stages=3-4 with block_K=64/128, traffic/launches each 1.2 as DRAM 34.6MB and block count dominate the observed ranking. Shared limit kept 32768 (hard portability cap binds). Next hypothesis: block_M=128/64 with block_N=128/256, block_K=64/128, stages=3-4, threads=128/256 to see if larger tiles with deeper K-pipelining beat 157.29us; validation scope note: Metal executed exact source/config/TIR numerics, CUDA binary not executed, GB10 latencies are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements.

Four attempts observed. Best is attempt-03 at 156.26 us (block_M=64,block_N=64,block_K=64,stages=2,threads=128,swizzle=4, smem=32768, 3 blocks/SM), slightly beating attempt-00 (157.29 us; block_M=128,block_N=64,block_K=64,stages=1,threads=256,swizzle=0, 2 blocks/SM). attempts-01/02 (block_M=32,block_N=128,block_K=32,stages=3,threads=256, swizzle 16 vs 64) both simulated 186.64 us with identical traffic/blocks-per-SM, so swizzle panel size produced no measurable latency change on this geometry and small-tile/short-block_K regime is rejected. All attempts compiled and passed numerics/SMT. Revision: drop block_M=16/32 and block_K=32/128-for-small-tiles; keep block_M=64/128, block_K=64/128, block_N=128/256 to test untested wider-N/fewer-launch and block_K=128 deeper-work hypotheses. Stages 2-4 (stage=1 was fast at attempt-00 but only with 256 threads; keep 2-4 to explore overlap). Threads 128/256 retained since 128 won attempt-03 and 256 won attempt-00 - feedback must disambiguate; swizzle trimmed to [0,4,8] since 16/64 were equivalent and M=128 gives at most 2 tile rows. Weights: footprint lowered to 0.6 (smem at cap but not the binding limiter), pipeline raised to 1.5 to favor deeper K-overlap, traffic/launches each 1.2 as DRAM 34.6MB and block count dominate. Shared limit stays 32768 (hard portability cap binds, actual smem 32768). Next hypothesis: block_M=64 with block_N=128/256, block_K=64/128, stages=3-4, threads=128/256, swizzle=0/4 to test whether wider N reduces launches enough to beat 156.26 us. Validation scope: Metal executed exact source/config/TIR numerics, CUDA binary not executed, GB10 latencies are simulator estimates only, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.

Attempt-04 was infeasible because the narrow domains combined with the 32768-byte cap left no allowed tuples once excluded configs were removed (block_N=[128,256] with block_M=[64,128], block_K=[64,128], stages 2-4 overshoot the estimate). Broaden to restore feasibility: add block_N=64 back (attempt-03 winner used block_N=64), widen block_K to include 64 only (128 kept for deeper-work test), and keep stages 1-4 (attempt-00 won at stage=1 with threads=256, attempt-03 won at stage=2 with threads=128; stage=1 should stay eligible). Best observed is attempt-03 at 156.26us (block_M=64,block_N=64,block_K=64,stages=2,threads=128,swizzle=4, 3 blocks/SM); attempt-00 close at 157.29us (block_M=128,block_N=64,block_K=64,stages=1,threads=256,swizzle=0). attempts-01/02 (block_M=32,block_N=128,block_K=32,stages=3,threads=256) both 186.64us identical across swizzle 16 vs 64, confirming small-tile/short-block_K regime is worse and panel swizzle gave no measurable gain there; drop block_M=16/32 and block_K=32. Swizzle trimmed to [0,4,8] since 16/64 were equivalent and M=128 gives at most 2 tile rows. Weights: pipeline raised to equal traffic/launches at 1.2 to keep stage choices competitive without over-bias; footprint dropped to 0.5 (smem pinned at cap and not the binding limiter in either winner). Next hypothesis: test block_M=64/128 with block_N=128/256 (wider N, fewer launches, still feasible via block_N=64 fallback) at block_K=64/128 to see if launch reduction beats 156.26us, and probe threads=128 vs 256 at deeper stages. Validation scope: Metal executed exact source/config/TIR numerics; CUDA binary not executed; GB10 latencies are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.

Five attempts observed. Best remains attempt-03 at 156.26us (block_M=64,block_N=64,block_K=64,stages=2,threads=128,swizzle=4, smem=32768, 3 blocks/SM); attempt-05 at 156.49us (block_M=64,block_N=128,block_K=64,stages=1,threads=256,swizzle=8, 2 blocks/SM) is essentially tied, so widening N with fewer stages/threads did not clearly beat it. attempt-00 = 157.29us; attempts-01/02 = 186.64us identically across swizzle 16 vs 64 confirming small-tile/short-block_K is worse and large panels give no measurable gain here. attempt-04 was infeasible from over-narrow domains. Latencies cluster tightly (~156-157us) for block_K=64 configs, so the binding constraint is roughly block_K=64 with M/near-cap smem; block_K=128 has not yet won. Revision: drop block_K=128 this round to avoid further MIP infeasibility at the 32768 cap and to concentrate on the competitive block_K=64 regime, keeping stages 1-4 and threads 128/256 since both produced near-tied winners and feedback must disambiguate. Retain block_M 64/128, block_N 64/128/256 to explore launch-vs-footprint trade-offs and enough tuples for feasibility after exclusions. Swizzle kept [0,4,8] since 16/64 were equivalent. Weights held near prior (traffic/launches/pipeline 1.2, footprint 0.5). Next hypothesis: thread=128/stages=1-2 vs thread=256/stages=1 at block_M=64/128, block_N=64/128, block_K=64 with swizzle=0/4 to test whether the near-tie resolves; if a block_K=128 test is desired later it may require reopening a broader feasible domain. Validation scope: Metal executed exact source/config/TIR numerics; CUDA binary not executed; GB10 latencies are simulator estimates only, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.

Six attempts observed. Best is attempt-03 at 156.26us (block_M=64,block_N=64,block_K=64,stages=2,threads=128,swizzle=4, smem=32768, 3 blocks/SM). attempt-05 and attempt-06 both simulated 156.49us (block_M=64,block_N=128,block_K=64, stages=1, threads=256, swizzle 8 then 4), essentially tied; attempts-00=157.29us; attempts-01/02=186.64us identically across swizzle 16 vs 64, confirming the small-tile/short-K regime is worse and large panels give no measurable gain here. All passed numerics/SMT and compiled. Latencies cluster tightly (~156-157us) for block_K=64, so block_K=64 is the competitive regime. Revision: previous attempt-06 dropped block_K=128, but the last two MIP rounds have repeatedly landed on the same block_K=64/stage=1-2/threads=256 near-tie; to break the plateau I reopen block_K=32 and block_N=32 (feasibility slack under the 32768 cap) while keeping block_K=64, and re-add threads=64 (unmeasured, a genuine warp-layout probe distinct from the 128-vs-256 tie). Keep block_M 64/128 and block_N up to 256 to test wider-N launch reduction. Swizzle reopened to full [0,4,8,16,32,64] but M=128 gives at most 2 tile rows for block_M=64, so panel gains are hypothesized small; instruction warns large panels may exceed cache, so lean on measured feedback rather than proxy. Weights held near prior (traffic/launches/pipeline 1.2, footprint 0.5) since footprint is pinned at cap and not the limiter. Shared limit stays 32768 (hard portability cap binds). Next hypothesis: test thread=64 and block_K=32 viability plus stage=3-4 at block_K=64 to see if any tuple beats 156.26us; if the plateau persists, accept the block_K=64 regime as the local floor. Validation scope: Metal executes exact source/config/TIR numerics; CUDA binary not executed; GB10 latencies are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.

Eight attempts observed. Best remains attempt-03 at 156.26us (block_M=64,block_N=64,block_K=64,stages=2,threads=128,swizzle=4, smem=32768, 3 blocks/SM). attempts 05/06/07 all simulated 156.49us at block_M=64,block_N=128,block_K=64,stages=1,threads=256 across swizzle 4/8/64, confirming swizzle panel changes above 4 give no measurable gain when M=128 limits reuse to at most 2 tile rows. attempts-01/02 (block_M=32,block_K=32,stages=3) were 186.64us and identical across swizzle 16/64, so small-tile/short-K is rejected. Latencies cluster tightly in 156-157us for block_K=64, indicating a plateau. Revision: drop block_K=32 and block_N=32 to stop spending rounds on losing/untested small-K regimes, and trim swizzle to [0,4] since 8/16/32/64 produced identical or no-gain outcomes. Keep block_M 64/128, block_N 64/128/256, block_K=64 (competitive regime), stages 1-3, and introduce threads=64 as the untested warp-layout probe alongside 128 (winner) and 256 (tied). Retaining block_N up to 256 tests launch reduction, block_N=64 retains the winner. Weights: traffic/launches/pipeline held at 1.0 to reduce arbitrary bias and let observed latency ranking drive selection; footprint lowered to 0.5 since smem is pinned at the 32768 portability cap and is not the binding limiter. Next hypothesis: threads=64 and stage=3 variants at block_M=64/128 with block_N=64/128 may break the 156.26us plateau; if not, accept block_K=64/stage=1-2 as the local floor. Validation scope: Metal executed exact source/config/TIR numerics; CUDA binary not executed; GB10 latencies are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.

Nine attempts observed. Best remains attempt-03 (block_M=64,block_N=64,block_K=64,stages=2,threads=128,swizzle=4, smem=32768, 3 blocks/SM) at 156.26us. attempts-05/06/07 all tie at 156.49us for block_M=64,block_N=128,block_K=64,stages=1,threads=256 across swizzle 4/8/64, so large panels give no measurable gain when M=128 limits reuse to <=2 tile rows. attempt-08 (block_M=64,block_N=128,block_K=64,stages=1,threads=128,swizzle=4) was slower at 157.64us with 132 registers, showing too few threads at stage=1 hurts. attempts-01/02 rejected the small-tile/short-K regime (186.64us). All attempts compiled, passed SMT and numerics. Revision: keep block_K=64 (the competitive regime; block_K=128 repeatedly drove MIP infeasibility at the 32768 cap and has never won), retain block_M 64/128 and block_N 64/128/256 for launch-vs-footprint trade-offs, and restrict threads to [128] since 256 tied but never beat 128 and 64 is unmeasured. Raise num_stages to [2,3,4] to test whether deeper K-pipelining at block_K=64 can break the 156.26us plateau (stage=1 with threads=128 lost in attempt-08), keeping the winning stage=2 tuple eligible. Swizzle trimmed to [0,4] since 8/16/32/64 were equivalent. Weights: pipeline raised to 1.3 to favor stage exploration, traffic/launches 1.2, footprint 0.5 since smem is pinned at the portability cap and not the binding limiter. Shared limit stays 32768 (hard portability cap binds). Next hypothesis: stages=3-4 with threads=128 at the winning block_M=64,block_N=64 tiles may beat 156.26us; block_M=128/block_N=64 alternate may tie. Validation scope: Metal executed exact source/config/TIR numerics; CUDA binary not executed; GB10 latencies are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.

Ten attempts observed (00-09): all feasible ones compiled, passed SMT and numerics; attempt-04 was infeasible from over-narrow domains. Best remains attempt-03 = 156.26us (block_M=64,block_N=64,block_K=64,stages=2,threads=128,swizzle=4, smem=32768, 3 blocks/SM); attempt-09 reproduced this tile/stage/thread at swizzle=0 for 156.259us (within noise; 8-byte estimate margin over the 32768 cap). attempts-05/06/07 tied at 156.49us for block_M=64,block_N=128,block_K=64,stages=1,threads=256 across swizzle 4/8/64, so larger panels give no measurable gain (M=128 with block_M=64 gives at most 2 tile rows; proxy reuse mispredicts here). attempt-08 (threads=128, stage=1) was slower at 157.64us with 132 registers, so 128 threads needs stage>=2. attempts-01/02 rejected small-tile/short-K (block_M=32,block_K=32) at 186.64us. Latencies are tightly clustered 156-157us in the block_K=64 regime, a plateau. Revision: reintroduce block_K=32 alongside 64 to have feasibility slack for larger tiles/stages under the 32768 cap and to probe whether a shorter K-step with deeper stages helps the 64-block_M regime; keep block_N 64 (winner) plus 128/256 for launch tests and block_M 64/128. Trim num_stages to [1,2,3] (stage=4 at block_K=64 tends to exceed cap or match lower stages) and swizzle to [0,4] since 8/16/32/64 were equivalent. Keep threads 128/256 (256 tied at stage=1, 128 won at stage=2; 64 never selected and untested). Weights: traffic/launches 1.1, pipeline 1.2 to keep stage exploration competitive, footprint 0.5 since smem is pinned at the portability cap and not the binding limiter. Shared limit stays 32768 (hard portability cap). Next hypothesis: block_M=64,block_N=64/128,block_K=64,stages=2/3,threads=128 vs 256 may break the plateau, and block_K=32 with stages=3 at wider N is a genuine structural alternative not yet tried. Validation scope: Metal executed exact source/config/TIR numerics; CUDA binary not executed; GB10 latencies are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.

Ten attempts observed; all feasible ones compiled, passed SMT and numerics (attempt-04 infeasible from over-narrow domains). Best is attempt-03/09 tie at 156.258us: block_M=64,block_N=64,block_K=64,stages=2,threads=128, swizzle 4 (03) and swizzle 0 (09, 156.2588us) essentially identical, so swizzle 0 vs 4 is within noise and panels >=8 gave no gain (05/06/07 tied 156.49us across swizzle 4/8/64 with M=128 limiting reuse to <=2 tile rows; proxy reuse overpredicts here). attempt-08 (stage=1,threads=128) slower 157.64us with 132 regs, so 128 threads needs stage>=2. attempt-10 (block_K=32,stages=2,threads=256) was 157.83us, so block_K=32 at this tile is not better. Revision: freeze the winning block_M=64, block_K=64 regime and focus remaining exploration narrowly — block_N in {64,128} (64 is winner; 128 tied at stage=1), stages in {2,3} (2 won; 3 untested at winner tile with 128 threads), threads 128/256 to disambiguate the tie, swizzle restricted to [4,8] to honor the instruction to keep swizzle exploration while acknowledging 0/4 equivalence. block_K=128 and stage=4 remain excluded because they repeatedly drive MIP infeasibility at the 32768 portability cap and have never won; the observed plateau (156.2-156.5us) suggests local floor. Weights: traffic 1.0, launches 1.1, pipeline 1.2 to favor stage comparison at the winning tile, footprint 0.5 since smem is pinned at the cap and not the binding limiter. Next hypothesis: stage=3 with threads=128 at block_M=64,block_N=64 may either break or confirm the 156.26us plateau; if it does not improve, accept block_K=64/stage=2/threads=128 as the local floor. Validation scope: Metal executed exact source/config/TIR numerics; CUDA binary not executed; GB10 latencies are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.
